correctness.rationale: The entire 2^15-edge-set complex was reconstructed twice by equivalent independent admissibility predicates; 4502 faces and all boundary-square-zero equations were checked. Exact signed integral elimination uses exclusively unit pivots with ranks (14,91,364,821,711,180), showing integral homology in degrees four and five only, of ranks 115 and 24. The 711-dimensional image of the degree-five boundary has an explicit integral unit-pivot basis; equivariant signed basis action on it yields exact integer traces for eleven S6 classes. A reversed-column independent basis reproduces these values. Equivariant Euler--Poincaré and exact rim-hook Specht characters give the claimed complete modules, with multiplicities passing orthogonality checks.

value.rationale: This is the first nontrivial n-3 bounded-domination graph complex singled out in the 2019 research problem; its previously known 115/24 sphere counts leave S6 symmetry completely undetermined. Identifying the 24-dimensional degree-five module as the trace-free tensor square of the standard five-dimensional representation is structurally compact, and the full degree-four decomposition determines all invariant homology and implies rational acyclicity of the quotient. These facts are neither automatic from dimension counts nor routine normalization tests.
